title: Check if Word Can Be Placed In Crossword
spaceBreakdown:
- string word: input, not counted
- a few int/bool locals: O(1)
- no containers allocated
approach: A valid placement must occupy a maximal run of non-`#` cells (in a row or column) whose length equals `word.length()`; the run is naturally bounded by `#` or the board edge, which enforces the "no empty/letter adjacent" rule. Scan every row for horizontal runs and every column for vertical runs. For each run of length `L == word.length()`, try matching the word forward and reversed (covering left-to-right/right-to-left and top-to-bottom/bottom-to-top). Return true on the first match.
hints: In the direction the word runs, what must be true of the cell immediately before the first letter and immediately after the last letter? The board has up to 2·10^5 cells, so checking every cell pair is too slow.

Scan each row and each column for maximal runs of non-`#` cells. For each run whose length equals `word.length()`, test the word forward and reversed against the run's cells. In Example 1, column 1 has the run `[' ',' ','c']` of length 3, and `"abc"` matches it top-to-bottom.

**Slot longer than word** - run length exceeds word length
`board = [[" "," "," "]], word = "ab"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking that the word matches a subsegment of the run instead of requiring equal length → returns `true`

**Reversed-only fit** - word matches only when reversed
`board = [["a","b"]], word = "ba"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: testing only the forward direction → returns `false`

**Letter mismatch inside slot** - run length is right but a letter disagrees
`board = [["a","b"]], word = "aa"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only run length, skipping the per-cell letter comparison → returns `true`

**Single-cell board** - m = n = 1
`board = [["a"]], word = "a"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: loop condition `j < n-1` or `i < m-1` that skips the last cell → returns `false`

followUps.q: Given a list of words, return all words that can be placed somewhere on the board.
followUps.a: Precompute every run (with its cells) once in O(m·n). For each word, test it against each run of matching length in both directions. Total time O(m·n + W·R) where R is the number of runs and W the word count; space stays O(1) beyond storing the runs if you keep them.

followUps.q: Place two given words simultaneously so they may share one crossing cell; is it possible?
followUps.a: Enumerate every valid placement of word A (position, direction, orientation) and every placement of word B as in the single-word solution, then check pairs whose perpendicular directions cross at exactly one cell where both letters agree. Time O(R_A·R_B) in the worst case with R_A, R_B the counts of valid placements; space O(R_A + R_B) to store candidate placements.

followUps.q: The board arrives row-by-row as a stream and you cannot store all of it; decide online whether the word fits.
followUps.a: Keep a sliding window of the last `word.length()` rows plus the current row's horizontal run state. Horizontal placements are decidable per row in O(n) memory; vertical placements need a buffer of the last `word.length()` rows (O(n·word.length()) memory) to test each column's recent run. Time stays O(m·n).
